description:
Leidos is actively interviewing for a Senior Hyperspectral Image Scientist to join our team in Springfield, VA. 
 Job Summary 
 Senior technical position responsible for leading the analysis, exploitation, and interpretation of hyperspectral and multispectral imagery in support of government missions. The Senior Hyperspectral Image Scientist will provide subject matter expertise in spectral data processing, algorithm development, image exploitation, and applied remote sensing science. This position requires on-site support at a government facility and close collaboration with analysts, engineers, program managers, and mission stakeholders.
 Primary Responsibilities 
 Lead the development, evaluation, and application of hyperspectral image analysis methodologies.

 Perform exploitation of hyperspectral, multispectral, and related geospatial datasets to identify, classify, and characterize materials, objects, and activities of interest.

 Develop, refine, and validate spectral-based algorithms for detection, unmixing, anomaly detection, change detection, target identification, and material classification.

 Conduct preprocessing and calibration workflows, including radiometric correction, atmospheric correction, and geometric correction.

 Build and maintain spectral libraries and support signature analysis, endmember extraction, and spectral matching.

 Integrate hyperspectral analytics with other GEOINT, remote sensing, and intelligence data sources.

 Prepare technical reports, briefings, white papers, and documentation for government stakeholders.

 Advise leadership and mission teams on capabilities, limitations, and best practices related to hyperspectral sensing and exploitation.

 Required Technical Skills 
 Hyperspectral and multispectral image exploitation

 Spectral signature analysis and spectral library development

 Material identification and classification

 Sub-pixel analysis and spectral unmixing

 Anomaly detection and change detection

 Radiometric, atmospheric, and geometric correction

 Algorithm development and validation

 Python, MATLAB, ENVI/IDL, GIS, and scientific scripting

 Data visualization and technical reporting

 Work Environment 
 Work will be performed primarily on-site at a government facility.

 Limited travel may be required based on program needs.

 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Remote Sensing, Imaging Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Geospatial Science, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

 Minimum of 8–12 years of relevant professional experience in hyperspectral image analysis, spectral science, remote sensing, or related technical disciplines.

 Demonstrated experience with hyperspectral and multispectral imagery exploitation in government, defense, intelligence, or applied research environments.

 Strong knowledge of spectral phenomenology, imaging spectroscopy, and remote sensing principles.

 Experience with image processing and scientific analysis tools such as MATLAB, Python, ENVI/IDL, ArcGIS, or equivalent platforms.

 Experience developing and implementing algorithms for spectral detection, classification, target recognition, or anomaly detection.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 Active TS/SCI clearance with ability to be approved for a Poly

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Master’s degree or Ph.D. in a relevant scientific or engineering discipline.

 Experience supporting DoD, IC, NGA, NGA-related, or other federal mission environments.

 Familiarity with sensor calibration, atmospheric modeling, physics-based exploitation, and sensor phenomenology.

 Experience with machine learning or artificial intelligence methods applied to hyperspectral data.

 Experience working with large-scale datasets, cloud-based analytics, or high-performance computing environments.

 Knowledge of geospatial data standards, data fusion, and operational tasking workflows.
